Project: PAPER ARM / 305. Read inputs/scene.json and use the original synthetic references. Assemble and animate the two complete patterned paper links on the supplied stationary base. Match the cyan ground pivot to the cyan first-link pivot, join the two orange hinge markers, and make the magenta tip follow the visible endpoint loop. Infer physical pivot centers and link lengths from the source parts. Rotate rigid parts without stretching, repainting, changing their pattern or losing any portion of either link. Keep the ground pivot fixed, the shared hinge connected and both source links recognizable throughout. The elbow stays BELOW the line from the cyan ground pivot to the magenta tip. Maintain that side throughout; do not flip branches or snap through a different pose. The endpoint positions are public and reachable with a margin throughout the loop. Numeric source pivot coordinates and link lengths are not supplied. The signed elbow branch is +1 or -1 as given by elbow_branch: for ground g, elbow e and endpoint t, sign((t.x-g.x)*(e.y-g.y)-(t.y-g.y)*(e.x-g.x)) must equal elbow_branch in image coordinates (positive y down). Preserve the source link patterns and pivot markers. Link 2 is visually in front of link 1 at their shared hinge. Minor resampling and the stated pivot/joint tolerances are allowed. Canonical source-layer reconstruction uses an inverse affine rigid-rotation mapping with bicubic resampling and source-over alpha composition. Other visually faithful sampling is permitted within the declared pixel and joint allowances. Deliver final.mp4: silent H.264, yuv420p, 800x544, 3 seconds, 12 fps, 36 indexed frames. Local Python standard libraries, Pillow and ffmpeg suffice. Preserve input bytes.

candidate-1.procedure:
Use a requirement-led render–inspect–repair checkpoint. Preserve the task requirements, immutable input bytes, current model, permissions, independent reviewer, four-review maximum and delivery policy.

Before rendering, record the required media properties, protected content, source-fidelity obligations and applicable spatial or temporal tolerances. Separate structural checks from content checks: a valid encode or successful render does not establish faithful artwork.

After each successful render, inspect the actual candidate, not an earlier preview. Check the full composition and source-comparison crops covering fine detail, repaired boundaries, moving artwork and crossings. For animation, decode every frame and verify its timestamp and content obligations; sampled contact sheets and playback supplement rather than replace these checks. Record which requirements were measured and which were only visually assessed.

When a defect appears, identify the affected requirement and distinguish geometry, source appearance, masking, compositing and encoding before making a narrowly scoped repair. Re-render and repeat affected checks plus protected-content regression checks. After a render failure, verify a fresh successful artifact before inspection or review; do not silently reuse a stale candidate.

Submit the frozen candidate to the independent reviewer with representative source comparisons and honest coverage limitations. A favorable visual verdict does not override a known content-check failure. Repair genuine discrepancies and revalidate within the existing four-review limit, without selecting evidence to conceal defects or changing acceptance criteria. Deliver the exact reviewed artifact according to the existing policy; any subsequent edit requires renewed validation and review within that limit.
candidate-1.hypothesis: Three animation runs failed both actors' source-pattern checks despite valid media structure and favorable sampled visual reviews. Adding explicit source-content and every-frame checkpoints will reduce this disagreement on comparable tasks. Test against baseline using unchanged independent checks: fewer delivered source-fidelity failures and reviewer false passes, with no regression in protected content, structural validity or review-limit compliance. The evidence does not establish a recurring render-failure problem; stale-artifact prevention is a conservative safeguard.

candidate-2.procedure:
Use a source-to-scene fidelity ledger for local repair and animation. Keep all task requirements, immutable sources, model, permissions, independent review, four-review limit and delivery policy unchanged.

For each source element, record its complete image extent, transparent padding, physical landmarks or pivots, permitted transform, trajectory and depth relationships. Distinguish canvas origin, visible silhouette bounds and physical anchors; cropping must not silently change the placement origin. Prefer supplied complete transparent assets over recreating artwork. Compare transformed patterns and proportions directly with their sources rather than accepting recognizable silhouettes alone.

For local restoration, establish source-to-target geometry from intact correspondences before transferring detail. Preserve target perspective and confine replacement to the authorized mask. Verify registration, boundary continuity, fine lettering and texture, and measure protected pixels outside the mask. The restoration evidence shows no recurring weakness, so retain this successful discipline rather than introducing broader reconstruction.

For flattened foreground occluders, derive local masks from the depth guide and connected outlined contours, not shared pigment alone. Inspect mask overlays at overlap regions; keep unrelated background artwork excluded. Preserve source alpha and transparent padding, use the required layer order and faithful source-over composition, and restrict edge handling to the task's disclosed allowance.

For articulated parts, infer physical pivot centers and lengths from the source, retain complete rigid parts, and use the specified signed branch in image coordinates. Check fixed anchors, connected joints, endpoint tracking, branch continuity and hinge-layer order at every frame. These examples passed, so treat these checks as conservative preservation, not evidence of a recurring linkage defect.

Evaluate public motion at every declared frame time. Verify source origin, scale and anchor placement before tuning masks or encoding. For every frame, check visible source-pattern fidelity separately from actual overlap depth, transparent padding and stationary background. Inspect the decoded deliverable as well as pre-encode frames to distinguish construction errors from encoding changes. If patterns disagree while depth checks succeed, investigate source selection, geometry, sampling and alpha handling without assuming the mask is at fault; the supplied evidence does not identify the exact cause.
candidate-2.hypothesis: The recurring animation weakness is visible actor-source fidelity, not demonstrated depth-order or padding failure: three runs failed both actor-pattern checks while those other checks passed. Explicit source-origin, anchor, transform and alpha checks should lower actor-region errors without degrading occlusion or stationary artwork. Compare baseline and this procedure on equivalent tasks using unchanged every-frame checks; the hypothesis is falsified if actor fidelity does not improve or gains require regressions elsewhere. No causal claim about the original implementation is assumed.
